strengths: Strong empirical results with 91% IoU@1 improvement over Point-SAM and 20%+ gains over SOTA on automatic segmentation across multiple benchmarks
Well-motivated problem: clearly identifies key limitations of prior work (clustering-based controllability, 2D-lifting surface-only understanding), with effective demonstration in Figure 2
Innovative model-in-the-loop data curation pipeline that scales from 180k to 500k shapes by leveraging PartField outputs with PartSAM interactive filtering, producing 5M+ shape-part pairs
Thoughtful dual-branch architecture design that elegantly preserves SAM's 2D priors (frozen branch) while learning 3D representations (learnable branch with auxiliary inputs)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including ablations on encoder variants and training data, fair evaluation choices (disabling mesh connectivity), both interactive and automatic segmentation modes, and additional applications
Demonstrates clear advantages on practically important scenarios (AI-generated shapes lacking connectivity, interior structure segmentation) where prior methods fail
Clear presentation with good motivation, effective figures, and honest discussion of limitations
weaknesses: Limited architectural novelty: encoder largely reuses PartField, triplane representation is from prior work, decoder is straightforward SAM adaptation; main novelty is in training paradigm and data rather than novel network design

Circular dependency and data quality concerns: relies on PartField for pseudo-labeling in stage 2 to train a model that outperforms PartField; critical details missing including fraction from stage 1 vs stage 2, pseudo-label quality analysis, sensitivity to IoU thresholds, and systematic validation of annotation noise

Limited generalization analysis: evaluation concentrated on Objaverse-based data (PartObjaverse-Tiny, ABO, Objaverse, AI-generated); no evaluation on real-world captured 3D data (ScanNet, real scans) or significantly different domains, reducing confidence in broad applicability

Mesh connectivity evaluation raises fairness questions: PartField drops 27% when connectivity disabled (79.2→51.5), yet paper disables it for PartField baseline in main comparison; results both ways should be shown explicitly

Reproducibility limited: code/model unavailable ('will be released soon'), model-in-the-loop pipeline lacks detailed algorithmic description, no statistics on filtering rates, and no error bars or significance testing on quantitative results

Missing ablations and analysis: no study of learnable branch alone vs. dual-branch, loss component contributions not ablated, failure modes not systematically analyzed, sensitivity to hyperparameters (IoU thresholds, NMS T) not explored
Unexplored design choices: IoU thresholds for model-in-the-loop filtering (60/90) appear arbitrary without justification or sensitivity analysis
